content.text:
I reviewed the first-party code (`index.js` and `lib/sanitize.js` — the only shipped source files; `test/test.js` is tests, not shipped logic). There's no file I/O, child process execution, SQL, templating, XML parsing, or outbound network calls in this package, so most of the requested categories don't apply. I found two concrete issues in the sanitization logic itself and recorded them in `findings.json`:

1. **CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion)** — `sanitize()` recurses into nested arrays/objects with no depth limit, and is run on attacker-controlled `req.body`/`req.query`/`req.params`/`req.headers`. A small deeply-nested JSON payload can exhaust the call stack and throw mid-request, enabling a DoS.
2. **CWE-79 (XSS filter bypass)** — `allowedKeys` is matched by key name only, applied identically at every nesting depth (the same options object is reused on every recursive call). An attacker who controls the shape of the JSON payload can nest a property with the same name as any configured `allowedKeys` entry anywhere in the tree to skip sanitization for that value, defeating the intended scope of the allow-list.
